sources.entry: Canary Tokens - Generates lightweight, embedded honeypot triggers called canary tokens for detecting unauthorized access. (Source Code) BSD-3-Clause Docker/Python

summary.one_liner: OpenCanary is an open-source, multi-protocol network honeypot that mimics network services and sends alerts when attackers interact with it inside non-public networks.
summary.what_it_does: OpenCanary runs as a daemon (opencanaryd) and emulates several common network protocols that attackers may probe after breaching a network. When something interacts with these decoy services, it sends alerts through configurable mechanisms, highlighting the source IP address. Configuration is a JSON file (opencanary.conf) where you enable protocol modules and alerting. Optional modules include SNMP (requires Scapy), Portscan (Linux only, uses iptables), and a Windows File Share module (smb, requires Samba). The README says it is written in Python, has low resource needs, and can run on a Raspberry Pi. It can be run directly on Linux or macOS, under pkgx, with Docker Compose, or with Docker.
use_cases: detect attackers inside a internal network
deploy a low-cost honeypot on a Raspberry Pi or small VM
alert on port scans against non-public hosts
decoy SNMP or file share services to catch intruders
run a network honeypot in Docker
how_to_run: Edit /etc/opencanaryd/opencanary.conf to enable the desired services and alerting
docker compose up latest (see Docker section of README)
notable: Multi-protocol honeypot with a JSON config file and modular services
Runs on low-resource hardware such as a Raspberry Pi
Drops root privileges after binding ports via --uid/--gid flags
Open-source edition of the commercial Thinkst Canary honeypot
caveats: Portscan module is Linux-only and needs iptables (not nftables); it is disabled in Docker
Windows File Share (smb) module is not available on macOS and needs Samba
Config file is read as root and should be root-owned to avoid privilege escalation
